subject: maths
title: Year 3 Tenths and Adding Fractions
seo_title: Year 3 Tenths and Adding Fractions Worksheets: Counting in Tenths, Tenths of Amounts (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Count up and down in tenths; recognise that tenths arise from dividing an object into 10 equal parts and in dividing one-digit numbers or quantities by 10; add and subtract fractions with the same denominator within one whole [for example, 5/7 + 1/7 = 6/7].
meta_desc: Free Year 3 maths worksheets on tenths for the National Curriculum: tenths of a shape, counting up and down in tenths, tenths of amounts, dividing by 10, and adding and subtracting fractions within one whole. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: A tenth is 1 of 10 equal parts. To add fractions with the same denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator.
body_html:
What is a tenth?

Split 1 whole into 10 equal parts. Each part is one tenth: 110. The parts must be the same size.

Counting in tenths

Count up in tenths by adding 1 to the numerator. The denominator stays 10. When you get to 1010, you have 1 whole. Then keep going: 1 110, 1 210 …

Example

Count down in tenths: 1 110, 1, ?

1 whole is 1010. One tenth less is 910.

Answer: 910

In Year 4 you will also write tenths as decimals: 310 = 0.3.

Tenths of amounts

To find 110 of a number, divide by 10.

Example

What is 310 of 40?

40 ÷ 10 = 4 for one tenth. Three tenths: 4 × 3 = 12.

Answer: 12

Dividing a one-digit number by 10 gives tenths. Share 3 cakes between 10 children: each child gets 310 of a cake. So 3 ÷ 10 = 310.

Adding and subtracting fractions

When the denominators are the same, the parts are the same size. Add or subtract the numerators. Keep the denominator.

Example

910 − 410 = ?

Subtract the numerators: 9 − 4 = 5. The parts are still tenths.

Answer: 510

Example

1 − 38 = ?

1 whole = 88. Then 8 − 3 = 5.

Answer: 58

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the denominators: 27 + 37 = 514Keep the denominator: 27 + 37 = 57
Counting 910, 1010, 1110 and not seeing the whole1010 is 1 whole: 910, 1, 1 110
110 of 30 = 300A tenth is smaller. Divide by 10: 30 ÷ 10 = 3
3 ÷ 10 = 103The number you divide goes on top: 3 ÷ 10 = 310
Counting the tick marks on a number line, not the spacesCount the jumps from 0

faq.q: What fractions do Year 3 children learn?
faq.a: In Year 3 children count up and down in tenths, find fractions of amounts, find equivalent fractions with diagrams, compare fractions, and add and subtract fractions with the same denominator within one whole, such as 5/7 + 1/7 = 6/7.

faq.q: How do you count in tenths?
faq.a: Add one tenth each time: 7/10, 8/10, 9/10, 1, 1 1/10. Ten tenths make 1 whole, so 10/10 is written as 1.

faq.q: How do you find a tenth of a number?
faq.a: Divide the number by 10. For example, 1/10 of 30 is 30 ÷ 10 = 3, and 3/10 of 30 is 3 × 3 = 9.

faq.q: Why don’t you add the denominators when adding fractions?
faq.a: The denominator tells you the size of the parts, and adding does not change their size. 2/7 + 3/7 is 5 sevenths, so the answer is 5/7, not 5/14.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 110. 3 parts are shaded. So 310 is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 110. 7 parts are shaded. So 710 is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: The bar has 10 equal parts, so each part is 110. 1 part is shaded. So 110 is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is not shaded?
items.e: 2 parts out of 10 are shaded, so 10 − 2 = 8 parts are not shaded. That is 810.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is not shaded?
items.e: 5 parts out of 10 are shaded, so 10 − 5 = 5 parts are not shaded. That is 510.

items.q: Which bar is split into tenths?
items.e: Tenths are 10 equal parts. Bar B has 10 parts that are all the same size. One bar has 10 parts, but they are not equal, so they are not tenths.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 9. There are 10 equal parts in the bar. So 910 is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the bar is shaded?
items.e: Count the shaded parts: 4. There are 10 equal parts in the bar. So 410 is shaded.

items.q: What fraction of the chocolate bar is shaded?
items.e: The chocolate bar has 10 equal pieces, so each piece is 110. 3 pieces are shaded: 310.

items.q: What fraction of the chocolate bar is shaded?
items.e: The chocolate bar has 10 equal pieces, so each piece is 110. 7 pieces are shaded: 710.

items.q: What fraction of the chocolate bar is not shaded?
items.e: There are 10 pieces and 6 are shaded. 10 − 6 = 4 pieces are not shaded: 410.

items.q: What fraction of the pizza is shaded?
items.e: The pizza is cut into 10 equal slices, so each slice is 110. 4 slices are shaded: 410.

items.q: What fraction of the pizza is shaded?
items.e: The pizza is cut into 10 equal slices, so each slice is 110. 8 slices are shaded: 810.

items.q: What fraction of the pizza is not shaded?
items.e: There are 10 slices and 7 are shaded. 10 − 7 = 3 slices are not shaded: 310.

items.q: How do you say 710?
items.e: The denominator 10 tells you the parts are tenths. The numerator tells you how many: 710 = seven tenths.

items.q: How do you say 310?
items.e: The denominator 10 tells you the parts are tenths. The numerator tells you how many: 310 = three tenths.

items.q: How many tenths make 1 whole?
items.e: 1 whole split into 10 equal parts gives 10 tenths: 1010 = 1.

items.q: A bar has 10 equal parts. How many parts do you shade to show 610?
items.e: The numerator tells you how many parts to shade: 6 of the 10 parts.

items.q: A bar has 10 equal parts. How many parts do you shade to show 810?
items.e: The numerator tells you how many parts to shade: 8 of the 10 parts.

items.q: A bar has 10 equal parts. What fraction is one part?
items.e: 1 part out of 10 equal parts is one tenth: 110.

sets.title: Count up and down in tenths

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 10 equal spaces, so each space is 110. Count the spaces from 0 to the dot: 3. The dot is at 310.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 10 equal spaces, so each space is 110. Count the spaces from 0 to the dot: 7. The dot is at 710.

items.q: What fraction is at the red dot?
items.e: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 10 equal spaces, so each space is 110. Count the spaces from 0 to the dot: 5. The dot is at 510.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: The big marks are 0, 1 and 2. Each small space is 110. The dot is past 1, and 3 more tenths. So it is at 1 310.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: The big marks are 0, 1 and 2. Each small space is 110. The dot is past 1, and 6 more tenths. So it is at 1 610.

items.q: What number is at the red dot?
items.e: The big marks are 0, 1 and 2. Each small space is 110. The dot is past 1, and 8 more tenths. So it is at 1 810.

items.q: What is 1 tenth more than 610?
items.e: Add 1 to the numerator: 610 + 110 = 710. The denominator stays 10.

items.q: What is 1 tenth less than 1?
items.e: 1 = 1010. Take away 1 tenth: 1010 − 110 = 910.

sets.title: Tenths of amounts and dividing by 10

items.q: Find 110 of 30.
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 30 ÷ 10 = 3. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 30.

items.q: Find 110 of 50.
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 50 ÷ 10 = 5. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 50.

items.q: Find 110 of 80.
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 80 ÷ 10 = 8. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 80.

items.q: Find 110 of 20.
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 20 ÷ 10 = 2. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 20.

items.q: What is 110 of 70?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 70 ÷ 10 = 7. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 70.

items.q: What is 110 of 40?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 40 ÷ 10 = 4. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 40.

items.q: What is 110 of 90?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 90.

items.q: What is 110 of 100?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 100 ÷ 10 = 10. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 100.

items.q: Find 310 of 40.
items.e: First find 110: 40 ÷ 10 = 4. Then take 3 of those parts: 4 × 3 = 12.

items.q: Find 710 of 20.
items.e: First find 110: 20 ÷ 10 = 2. Then take 7 of those parts: 2 × 7 = 14.

items.q: What is 210 of 50?
items.e: First find 110: 50 ÷ 10 = 5. Then take 2 of those parts: 5 × 2 = 10.

items.q: What is 410 of 60?
items.e: First find 110: 60 ÷ 10 = 6. Then take 4 of those parts: 6 × 4 = 24.
Share 3 wholes into 10 equal groups. Cut each whole into tenths: that makes 30 tenths. Each group gets 3 tenths. So 3 ÷ 10 = 310.
Share 7 wholes into 10 equal groups. Cut each whole into tenths: that makes 70 tenths. Each group gets 7 tenths. So 7 ÷ 10 = 710.
Share 9 wholes into 10 equal groups. Cut each whole into tenths: that makes 90 tenths. Each group gets 9 tenths. So 9 ÷ 10 = 910.
Share 4 wholes into 10 equal groups. Cut each whole into tenths: that makes 40 tenths. Each group gets 4 tenths. So 4 ÷ 10 = 410.

sets.title: Add and subtract fractions within one whole

items.q: 15 + 35 = ?
items.e: Count the coloured parts: 1 green and 3 yellow make 4 fifths. So 15 + 35 = 45.

items.q: 27 + 37 = ?
items.e: Count the coloured parts: 2 green and 3 yellow make 5 sevenths. So 27 + 37 = 57.

items.q: 38 + 48 = ?
items.e: Count the coloured parts: 3 green and 4 yellow make 7 eighths. So 38 + 48 = 78.

items.q: 410 + 510 = ?
items.e: Count the coloured parts: 4 green and 5 yellow make 9 tenths. So 410 + 510 = 910.

items.q: 56 − 26 = ?

items.q: 79 − 39 = ?

items.q: 810 − 510 = ?
items.e: 8 tenths are shaded and 5 are crossed out. 8 − 5 = 3 tenths are left: 310.

items.q: 19 + 59 = ?
items.e: The parts are all ninths. Add the numerators: 1 + 5 = 6. Keep the denominator 9. So 19 + 59 = 69, not 618.

items.q: 310 + 410 = ?
items.e: The parts are all tenths. Add the numerators: 3 + 4 = 7. Keep the denominator 10. So 310 + 410 = 710, not 720.

items.q: 26 + 36 = ?
items.e: The parts are all sixths. Add the numerators: 2 + 3 = 5. Keep the denominator 6. So 26 + 36 = 56, not 512.

items.q: 412 + 512 = ?
items.e: The parts are all twelfths. Add the numerators: 4 + 5 = 9. Keep the denominator 12. So 412 + 512 = 912, not 924.

items.q: 17 + 27 + 37 = ?
items.e: All the parts are sevenths. 1 + 2 + 3 = 6. Keep the denominator: 67.

items.q: 78 − 28 = ?
items.e: Subtract the numerators: 7 − 2 = 5. Keep the denominator: the parts are still eighths. So the answer is 58.

items.q: 910 − 610 = ?
items.e: Subtract the numerators: 9 − 6 = 3. Keep the denominator: the parts are still tenths. So the answer is 310.

items.q: 45 − 15 = ?
items.e: Subtract the numerators: 4 − 1 = 3. Keep the denominator: the parts are still fifths. So the answer is 35.

items.q: 1112 − 412 = ?
items.e: Subtract the numerators: 11 − 4 = 7. Keep the denominator: the parts are still twelfths. So the answer is 712.

items.q: 1 − 38 = ?

items.q: 1 − 410 = ?

items.q: A cake is cut into 8 equal slices. Aisha eats 2 slices and Harry eats 3 slices. What fraction of the cake do they eat altogether?
items.e: Each slice is 18. 2 + 3 = 5 slices, so they eat 58. Keep the denominator 8.

items.q: A chocolate bar has 10 equal pieces. Kai eats 410 of the bar. What fraction is left?
items.e: The whole bar is 1010. 1010 − 410 = 610 is left.

items.q: A race is 10 laps of the school field. Charlie has run 7 laps. What fraction of the race has he run?
items.e: Each lap is 110 of the race. 7 laps is 710.

items.q: A race is 10 laps. Zara has run 610 of the race. What fraction does she still have to run?
items.e: The whole race is 1010. 1010 − 610 = 410 is still to run.

items.q: A pizza is cut into 6 equal slices. Mohammed eats 16 of the pizza, then 26 more. How much does he eat altogether?
items.e: 1 + 2 = 3 sixths. The slices are still sixths, so the answer is 36, not 312.

items.q: Ava drinks 25 of a bottle of juice. Her friend drinks 15 of the bottle. What fraction of the juice is left?
items.e: They drink 25 + 15 = 35. The full bottle is 55. 55 − 35 = 25 is left.

items.q: A school garden has 9 equal beds. 49 of the garden has carrots and 39 has peas. What fraction of the garden has carrots or peas?
items.e: 4 + 3 = 7 ninths: 79. Keep the denominator 9.

items.q: Leo has 1 m of ribbon. He cuts off 310 m. How much ribbon is left?
items.e: 1 m = 1010 m. 1010 − 310 = 710 m.

items.q: There are 50 sweets in a jar. 110 of them are red. How many red sweets are there?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 50 ÷ 10 = 5 sweets. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 50.

items.q: There are 20 pupils in a group. 310 of them walk to school. How many pupils walk to school?
items.e: First find 110: 20 ÷ 10 = 2. Then take 3 of those parts: 2 × 3 = 6 pupils.

items.q: Two chocolate bars are shared equally between 10 children. How much does each child get?
c: 210 of a bar
102 of a bar
12 of a bar
110 of a bar
items.e: 2 ÷ 10 = 210. Each child gets 210 of a bar.

items.q: Freya says 27 + 37 = 514. What went wrong?
items.e: The parts are sevenths, and they stay sevenths. Add only the numerators: 2 + 3 = 5. So 27 + 37 = 57.

items.q: Grace reads 29 of her book on Monday and 49 on Tuesday. What fraction of the book has she read?
items.e: 2 + 4 = 6 ninths: 69. Keep the denominator 9.

items.q: A tower has 10 cubes. 4 cubes are red and 3 cubes are blue. The rest are white. What fraction of the tower is red or blue?
items.e: Red: 410. Blue: 310. 410 + 310 = 710.

items.q: A cake is cut into 12 equal slices. 712 of the cake is eaten at a party. What fraction is left?
items.e: The whole cake is 1212. 1212 − 712 = 512 is left.

items.q: Lily has 38 of a pizza. Evie has 58 of the same pizza. How much more does Evie have?
items.e: Find the difference: 58 − 38 = 28.

items.q: George colours 410 of a picture in the morning and 510 after lunch. What fraction is not coloured yet?
items.e: 410 + 510 = 910 is coloured. 1010 − 910 = 110 is not coloured yet.

items.q: Ethan has a ribbon 90 cm long. He cuts off 110 of it. How long is the piece he cuts off?
items.e: To find 110, divide by 10: 90 ÷ 10 = 9 cm. It is one of 10 equal parts, so it is smaller than 90.

items.q: There are 30 cubes in a box. 410 of them are red. How many red cubes are there?
items.e: First find 110: 30 ÷ 10 = 3. Then take 4 of those parts: 3 × 4 = 12 cubes.

items.q: Jack cuts a 1 m plank of wood into 10 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Each piece is 110 of 1 m: 100 ÷ 10 = 10 cm.
